## bf1bc9d143b8

**Issue found: vertical behavior and crossing precedence are not intentionally taught, and the prose summary contradicts the selected rule at a conflicting cross.** Every canonical training input contains one horizontal and one vertical fill. Ordinary generation explicitly places only horizontal triplets; vertical cases occur accidentally.

Across 600 ordinary samples, the probe found 1,461 horizontal centers but only 11 vertical-only centers in 7 samples and one crossing center in one sample. Thus a horizontal-only learner sees no vertical witness in roughly 98.8% of individual generated inputs, and there is no schedule guaranteeing one in a lesson.

There is also an exact precedence disagreement. On:

```text
020
303
020
```

the center is bracketed horizontally by `3` and vertically by `2`. The generator `SUMMARY` says horizontal precedence, which predicts center `3`. The selected Racket control flow makes its horizontal branch false when both matches exist with different colors, then takes the vertical branch, yielding center `2`. The ordinary generator does not intentionally emit this disambiguating case.

The task should either define and test the selected vertical precedence, or change the authority to the documented horizontal precedence; then schedule horizontal-only, vertical-only, same-color crossing, and conflicting-color crossing witnesses. The linter independently reports a missing `RULE_HASH` and two unprobeable singleton axes.

triage.reason: Both source-bound finding sections retained for future task owners. Local main-generator checks do not independently reproduce these audits. See REVIEW/intake-20261002-batch12.json.
